questions.subject: English Studies
questions.learningObjective: Locate information and make supported inferences from a passage.
questions.prompt: What was the main difference in the treatment of the two containers?
questions.answer: The amount of light available to them.
questions.explanation: One container was by a sunny window and the other was in a dark cupboard; soil and watering were kept alike.
options: The amount of light available to them.
questions.passage: The Primary Six class planted beans in two identical containers. Both containers held the same type and amount of soil, and both received equal amounts of water. The class placed one container near a sunny window and the other in a dark cupboard. After several days, the seedlings in the cupboard were pale and thin, while those near the window were greener. The pupils recorded the changes instead of pulling up the seedlings each day. Their teacher reminded them that a fair comparison required more than noticing one difference: they also needed to keep the other important conditions alike. The class decided to repeat the investigation before writing its final report.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Technology
questions.learningObjective: Explain elementary life processes and environmental relationships.
questions.prompt: Why do green plants need sunlight?
questions.answer: It supplies energy for making food during photosynthesis.
questions.explanation: Light provides energy; it is not a mineral taken up by the roots.
options: It provides the carbon atoms in glucose directly.
It supplies energy for making food during photosynthesis.
It replaces all water absorbed by roots.
It makes soil unnecessary for every kind of plant.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Technology
questions.learningObjective: Explain elementary life processes and environmental relationships.
questions.prompt: Which part of a flowering plant takes in most water from the soil?
questions.answer: Roots.
questions.explanation: Roots, particularly their root hairs, absorb water from soil.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Technology
questions.learningObjective: Explain elementary life processes and environmental relationships.
questions.prompt: Which sequence shows the usual main stages in a butterfly’s life cycle?
questions.answer: Egg → larva → pupa → adult.
questions.explanation: A butterfly undergoes complete metamorphosis with a caterpillar larva and a pupal stage.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Technology
questions.learningObjective: Explain elementary life processes and environmental relationships.
questions.prompt: Which meal supplies both an energy-giving staple and a protein-rich food?

questions.explanation: Rice supplies mainly carbohydrate, while beans contribute protein as well as other nutrients.

questions.learningObjective: Explain elementary life processes and environmental relationships.
questions.prompt: Why are teeth of different shapes useful?
questions.answer: Different shapes help cut, tear and grind food.
questions.explanation: Incisors, canines and broad back teeth have different forms suited to different actions.
options: Tooth shape has no connection with chewing.
Different shapes help cut, tear and grind food.
Every tooth is used only to taste sweetness.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Technology
questions.learningObjective: Explain elementary life processes and environmental relationships.
questions.prompt: Which organism is a producer in a simple pond food chain?
questions.answer: Green algae.
questions.explanation: Green algae can make organic food using light and provide food for consumers.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Technology

questions.prompt: Why should a school avoid removing every flowering plant from its garden?
questions.answer: Some insects depend on flowers for nectar and pollen.
questions.explanation: Flowering plants provide resources for pollinating insects and help support garden food relationships.
options: Flowers prevent all insects from reproducing.
Every flower makes the soil poisonous.
Only stones can support living things.
Some insects depend on flowers for nectar and pollen.

Both wires attached only to the same cell terminal.
A bulb connected only to a dry wooden stick.
A complete conducting path between the cell terminals through the bulb.

options: Light bends around every object completely.
Shadows form only when no light source exists.
The object blocks light travelling from the source.
The object produces darkness as a liquid.

questions.subject: Reading and Writing
questions.learningObjective: Draw warranted conclusions from short texts and data.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
questions.answer: A change in scheduling made an existing resource more accessible.
questions.explanation: The text attributes improved access to different opening hours rather than new equipment or a larger collection.
options: A change in scheduling made an existing resource more accessible.
A larger budget always improves a library’s collection.
Students prefer digital books in every subject.
Libraries should remove all quiet study areas.
questions.passage: A university library bought no new computers during the spring term. Instead, it opened its computer room earlier on examination days. Morning attendance increased, especially among commuters who had previously arrived before the room opened.

questions.subject: Reading and Writing
questions.learningObjective: Draw warranted conclusions from short texts and data.
questions.prompt: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the researchers’ proposed explanation?
questions.answer: Seeds exposed to the same moisture but different temperatures germinate at different rates.
questions.explanation: Controlling moisture while varying temperature directly tests whether temperature can account for the germination-rate difference.
options: The seeds all came from plants with the same flower colour.
The laboratory shelves were repainted before the study.
Researchers wrote their notes using different pens.
Seeds exposed to the same moisture but different temperatures germinate at different rates.
questions.passage: Researchers observed that seeds on a warm windowsill germinated sooner than seeds in a cool room. They proposed that temperature, rather than differences in watering, explained the contrast. A follow-up experiment would need to separate those factors.

questions.subject: Reading and Writing
questions.learningObjective: Draw warranted conclusions from short texts and data.
questions.prompt: Which conclusion is best supported by the text?
questions.answer: The surveys do not establish that the new pavement caused all of the change in walking.
questions.explanation: Two conditions changed together, and the observational comparison does not isolate the pavement’s causal contribution.
options: Every resident walked more after the change.
Traffic levels remained identical throughout both surveys.
The surveys do not establish that the new pavement caused all of the change in walking.
New pavement can never affect walking behaviour.
questions.passage: After a town widened its pavements, a survey recorded more walking trips. During the same period, several employers introduced flexible hours. The transport team noted both changes and described the survey as evidence of a trend, not a controlled experiment.

questions.subject: Reading and Writing
questions.learningObjective: Draw warranted conclusions from short texts and data.
questions.prompt: Which observation from the text provides the strongest evidence that the containers reduced water loss?
questions.answer: Covered containers lost less mass than uncovered containers under the same conditions.
questions.explanation: The controlled mass comparison is direct evidence of lower water loss; labels and appearance are not equivalent measurements.
options: A researcher photographed the room before weighing.
Covered containers lost less mass than uncovered containers under the same conditions.
The containers were labelled with permanent ink.
The containers were placed on a wooden bench.
questions.passage: A researcher placed equal volumes of water in identical containers. Half were covered and half left uncovered in the same room. After two days, the covered containers had lost less mass. Labels and photographs helped document the procedure, but mass measurements supplied the key evidence.

questions.subject: Reading and Writing
questions.learningObjective: Draw warranted conclusions from short texts and data.
questions.prompt: Which statement accurately interprets the table described in the text?
questions.answer: Attendance rose by more people in June than in May.
questions.explanation: May gained 10 people and June gained 30, so the larger numerical increase occurred in June.
options: Attendance rose by more people in June than in May.
June had fewer attendees than April.
questions.passage: A museum recorded 120 visitors in April, 130 in May, and 160 in June. The figures represent monthly attendance counts, not percentages. Staff wanted to describe how the size of the month-to-month increase changed over the period.

questions.subject: Reading and Writing
questions.learningObjective: Interpret words and rhetorical choices in context.
questions.prompt: As used in the text, “tentative” most nearly means
questions.answer: provisional.
questions.explanation: The team awaits further measurements, so its explanation is not yet treated as established.
questions.passage: The team offered a tentative explanation for the unusual mineral pattern. Although the explanation fitted the first set of samples, the researchers planned additional measurements before deciding whether it could account for deposits across the entire region.

questions.subject: Reading and Writing
questions.learningObjective: Interpret words and rhetorical choices in context.
questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the second sentence?
questions.answer: To provide a specific example of the general claim in the first sentence.
questions.explanation: The invented example illustrates how design details can influence use; it does not refute the broader claim.
options: To introduce an unrelated historical period.
To show that every visitor has the same preferences.
To provide a specific example of the general claim in the first sentence.
To deny that design can affect behaviour.
questions.passage: Small design choices can influence how public spaces are used. In one community garden, benches placed beside the entrance attracted brief conversations, whereas seats along the quieter rear path were used more often for solitary reading.

questions.subject: Reading and Writing
questions.learningObjective: Interpret words and rhetorical choices in context.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the relationship between the two texts?
questions.answer: Text 2 qualifies Text 1’s proposal by identifying a condition that may limit its effect.
questions.explanation: The second text accepts a possible benefit but notes that affordability also matters, narrowing the first text’s general recommendation.
options: Both texts claim that cost can never affect ridership.
Text 2 qualifies Text 1’s proposal by identifying a condition that may limit its effect.
Text 2 proves that every claim in Text 1 is false.
Text 2 discusses an entirely unrelated form of transport.
questions.passage: Text 1: Extending evening bus services could make cultural events accessible to more residents. Text 2: Later buses may help, but the benefit will be limited for residents who still cannot afford the fare.

questions.subject: Reading and Writing
questions.learningObjective: Interpret words and rhetorical choices in context.
questions.prompt: As used in the text, “exacting” most nearly means
questions.answer: demanding great care.
questions.explanation: The description of alignment and precision establishes the meaning of exacting in the context of the work.
questions.passage: The restoration was exacting work. Each narrow strip of paper had to be aligned with the surviving pattern, and even a small shift could distort the image. The conservator therefore paused frequently to check the placement.

questions.subject: Reading and Writing
questions.learningObjective: Interpret words and rhetorical choices in context.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the function of the final sentence?
questions.answer: It cautions against treating one explanation as sufficient.
questions.explanation: The final sentence introduces other causes that complicate a single-factor account of migration.
options: It proves the opening observation never occurred.
It defines a term unrelated to migration.
It claims that food availability has no possible effect.
It cautions against treating one explanation as sufficient.
questions.passage: The birds arrived earlier during years with abundant insects. This pattern suggested that food availability might influence migration timing. However, weather along the migration route and conditions at nesting sites could also contribute to the observed differences.

questions.subject: Reading and Writing
questions.learningObjective: Choose revisions that meet a stated rhetorical goal.
questions.prompt: Which transition most logically completes the text?
questions.answer: However,
questions.explanation: The second sentence introduces a limitation to the first sentence’s favourable observation, so a contrast is needed.
questions.passage: The compact filter removed most visible particles from the water during the trial. ___, the researchers emphasised that clarity alone did not establish that the filtered water was free of dissolved contaminants.

questions.subject: Reading and Writing
questions.learningObjective: Choose revisions that meet a stated rhetorical goal.
questions.prompt: Which transition best shows that the final sentence is a consequence of the preceding information?
questions.answer: Consequently,
questions.explanation: The shortage of suitable storage is presented as a reason for changing the delivery schedule.
questions.passage: The archive received several large collections in a single month. Its existing storage rooms were already nearly full. ___, staff postponed a planned delivery until an additional room could be prepared.

questions.subject: Reading and Writing
questions.learningObjective: Choose revisions that meet a stated rhetorical goal.
questions.prompt: A student wants to emphasise a similarity between the two projects. Which sentence best uses the notes?
questions.answer: Both projects enlisted volunteers to record observations over time.
questions.explanation: The sentence selects the shared feature and avoids falsely equating the projects’ subjects or locations.
options: Both projects enlisted volunteers to record observations over time.
Only the river project involved any volunteers.
The bird project measured river depth every week.
The two projects studied identical animal populations.
questions.passage: Notes: A river project trained volunteers to record water levels weekly. A bird project asked volunteers to count birds monthly. The projects operated in different regions. Both kept repeated records to support long-term comparisons.

questions.subject: Reading and Writing
questions.learningObjective: Choose revisions that meet a stated rhetorical goal.
questions.prompt: A student wants to explain why the second trial used smaller packets. Which sentence most effectively meets that goal?
questions.answer: Because large packets often remained unfinished, the second trial tested smaller portions.
questions.explanation: The sentence connects the observed waste in the first trial to the change in portion size in the second.
options: The second trial happened after the first trial.
The labels were printed in blue ink during both trials.
Several packets were placed in a cupboard before distribution.
Because large packets often remained unfinished, the second trial tested smaller portions.
questions.passage: Notes: Participants in the first food trial often left part of each large packet uneaten. The second trial offered smaller packets. Labels and distribution times were unchanged. Researchers compared the amount left over after each trial.

questions.subject: Reading and Writing
questions.learningObjective: Choose revisions that meet a stated rhetorical goal.
questions.prompt: Which revision would best introduce the text’s central contrast?
questions.answer: The new method saved time but required more preparation.
questions.explanation: The remainder contrasts shorter measurement time with longer setup, so the introduction should forecast both sides.
options: Both methods used exactly the same amount of time at every stage.
The researchers measured the room before buying a table.
The new method saved time but required more preparation.
The new method eliminated every stage of preparation.
questions.passage: The researchers compared an automated method with manual recording. Once running, the automated method processed samples quickly. Before each run, however, staff had to spend considerably more time calibrating and checking the equipment than they had with the manual method.

questions.subject: Reading and Writing
questions.learningObjective: Edit grammar and punctuation in context.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to Standard English conventions?
questions.answer: samples were
questions.explanation: The subject samples is plural, and its intervening descriptive phrase does not change the verb agreement.
questions.passage: The mineral ___ stored in separate labelled bags before analysis. Each bag also contained a note identifying the collection site, allowing the laboratory team to compare chemical patterns across the valley.

questions.subject: Reading and Writing
questions.learningObjective: Edit grammar and punctuation in context.
questions.prompt: Which punctuation best joins the two independent clauses at the marked boundary?
questions.answer: a semicolon
questions.explanation: Both sides are complete independent clauses; a semicolon can join them without a coordinating conjunction.
questions.passage: The first sensor recorded temperature every minute [boundary] the second recorded it every ten minutes. Before combining the results, the team adjusted the data so that the different sampling intervals would not distort the comparison.

questions.subject: Reading and Writing
questions.learningObjective: Edit grammar and punctuation in context.
questions.prompt: Which choice correctly completes the possessive expression?
questions.answer: researcher’s
questions.explanation: The text refers to one researcher’s notebook, so singular possessive researcher’s is required.
questions.passage: One researcher kept a notebook throughout the expedition. The ___ notes included sketches of riverbanks, daily weather observations, and comments on equipment, providing a detailed record that later helped the team interpret its measurements.

questions.subject: Reading and Writing
questions.learningObjective: Edit grammar and punctuation in context.
questions.prompt: Which choice supplies the correct verb form in the text?
questions.answer: has examined
questions.explanation: Since 2021 describes a period extending to the present; the singular subject team takes has examined in this usage.
questions.passage: Since 2021, the team ___ a growing collection of soil samples from the same valley. Its latest report compares the new results with earlier measurements to identify changes that might otherwise be missed.

questions.subject: Reading and Writing
questions.learningObjective: Edit grammar and punctuation in context.
questions.prompt: Which choice makes the series grammatically parallel?
questions.answer: mapping habitats, counting nests, and recording rainfall
questions.explanation: All three coordinated activities use matching -ing forms.
options: habitat mapping, to counting nests, and records rainfall
mapping habitats, counting nests, and recording rainfall
mapping habitats, to count nests, and rainfall records
to mapping habitats, counting nests, and record rainfall
questions.passage: The field course introduced students to three connected activities: ___. By practising each activity in the same study area, students learned to connect information about vegetation, breeding birds, and seasonal water availability.

questions.subject: Reading and Writing
questions.learningObjective: Draw warranted conclusions from short texts and data.
questions.prompt: What inference about the two materials is best supported?
questions.answer: The trial suggests that insulation performance depends partly on the material’s structure, not only its thickness.
questions.explanation: Equal thickness but different cooling outcomes supports a structural contribution; the result does not establish universal rankings under every condition.
options: The trial suggests that insulation performance depends partly on the material’s structure, not only its thickness.
The two materials had identical internal structures.
Both containers gained heat at the same rate.
questions.passage: Two containers held equally hot water and were wrapped in insulation of the same thickness. One wrapping trapped many small pockets of air; the other was dense and smooth. Under the same room conditions, the first container cooled more slowly.

questions.subject: Reading and Writing
questions.learningObjective: Interpret words and rhetorical choices in context.
questions.prompt: As used in the text, “tempered” most nearly means
questions.answer: moderated.
questions.explanation: The concerns reduce the researchers’ confidence in the strong interpretation without erasing their interest in the result.
questions.passage: The unexpected improvement encouraged the researchers, but their enthusiasm was tempered by the small sample. They planned a larger trial before recommending the technique widely, acknowledging that promising early results can fail to persist.

questions.subject: Reading and Writing
questions.learningObjective: Choose revisions that meet a stated rhetorical goal.
questions.prompt: Which transition most appropriately introduces the added supporting point?
questions.answer: Moreover,
questions.explanation: The second sentence adds another benefit of the route rather than contrasting with or illustrating a different claim.
questions.passage: The new walking route connected two residential areas without requiring pedestrians to cross the main road. ___, it provided a shaded approach to the public library, making the trip more comfortable during the hottest part of the day.

questions.subject: Reading and Writing
questions.learningObjective: Edit grammar and punctuation in context.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with a clear and grammatically correct modifier?
questions.answer: After reviewing the measurements, the engineers revised the design.
questions.explanation: The engineers perform the reviewing, so they must be the subject modified by the introductory phrase.
options: After reviewing the measurements, several changes to the design were necessary.
After reviewing the measurements, the engineers revised the design.
After reviewing the measurements, the design was revised by the engineers.
After reviewing the measurements, the revised design lay on the table.
questions.passage: The measurements revealed that the original support would bend more than expected under the planned load. ___. Their next model used an additional brace, which they tested before approving the final plans.

questions.subject: Reading and Writing
questions.learningObjective: Draw warranted conclusions from short texts and data.
questions.prompt: Which statement would the author most likely agree with?
questions.answer: A useful model can simplify reality if its limitations remain explicit.
questions.explanation: The author values simplification for a stated purpose while warning against using a model beyond the conditions it represents.
options: A useful model can simplify reality if its limitations remain explicit.
Every useful model must include every real-world detail.
A model becomes useless as soon as it leaves out anything.
Limitations should be hidden to make a model persuasive.
questions.passage: A map omits most details of the landscape, yet it can guide a traveller effectively. Scientific models work similarly: their simplifications can clarify a relationship, provided users remember which conditions and features the model does not represent.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.learningObjective: Model and solve linear equations systems and inequalities.
questions.prompt: A service charges a fixed fee of $18 plus $7 per hour. Which equation gives total cost C for h hours?
questions.explanation: The fixed fee is added once and the hourly charge is multiplied by the number of hours.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.learningObjective: Model and solve linear equations systems and inequalities.
questions.prompt: For a line defined by 3x + 2y = 12, what is the y-intercept?
questions.explanation: At the y-intercept x = 0, so 2y = 12 and y = 6.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.learningObjective: Model and solve linear equations systems and inequalities.
questions.prompt: If 5x − 4 = 2x + 11, what is x?
questions.explanation: Subtract 2x and add 4 to obtain 3x = 15, giving x = 5.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.learningObjective: Model and solve linear equations systems and inequalities.
questions.prompt: A line has slope −2 and passes through (1, 5). Which equation represents it?
questions.explanation: Substitute the point into y = −2x+b: 5 = −2+b, so b = 7.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.learningObjective: Model and solve linear equations systems and inequalities.
questions.prompt: Which system has no solution?
questions.answer: y = 2x + 1 and y = 2x − 3
questions.explanation: The lines have equal slopes but different intercepts, so they are distinct and parallel.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.learningObjective: Analyse nonlinear functions and equivalent expressions.
questions.prompt: Which expression is equivalent to x² − 9 for every real x?
questions.explanation: The expression is a difference of squares.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.learningObjective: Analyse nonlinear functions and equivalent expressions.
questions.prompt: A population is modelled by P(t) = 800(1.05)^t. What does 1.05 indicate?
questions.answer: The model grows by 5% per time unit.
questions.explanation: A growth factor of 1.05 equals 1 plus a 0.05 proportional increase.
options: The model grows by 5% per time unit.
The population adds exactly 1.05 individuals per unit.
The population falls by 5% per unit.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.learningObjective: Analyse nonlinear functions and equivalent expressions.
questions.prompt: For f(x) = (x − 4)² + 3, what is the minimum value of f(x) over real x?
questions.explanation: A square is nonnegative and is zero at x = 4, leaving the minimum value 3.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.learningObjective: Analyse nonlinear functions and equivalent expressions.
questions.prompt: For x ≠ 3, which expression is equivalent to (x² − 9)/(x − 3)?
questions.explanation: Factor the numerator as (x−3)(x+3) and cancel the nonzero factor x−3.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.learningObjective: Interpret quantitative evidence and proportional relationships.
questions.prompt: A price increases by 20% and is then reduced by 20% of the new price. What is the net percentage change from the original?
questions.answer: A decrease of 4%.
questions.explanation: The multipliers are 1.2 and 0.8; their product is 0.96, or 4% below the original.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.learningObjective: Interpret quantitative evidence and proportional relationships.
questions.prompt: A randomly selected sample of 500 registered voters in a town is surveyed about a local proposal. To which group can the result most defensibly be generalised, assuming adequate response?
questions.answer: The town’s registered voters.
questions.explanation: The sampling frame defines the population represented; it does not automatically represent all children or every other town.
options: All visitors who have ever entered the town.
Only the 500 respondents, with no possibility of population inference.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.learningObjective: Interpret quantitative evidence and proportional relationships.
questions.prompt: The values in a data set are 2, 4, 4, 5 and 20. Which measure changes most directly because of the unusually large value 20?
questions.answer: The mean is pulled upward relative to the median.
questions.explanation: The mean uses every numerical value, whereas the median is the middle ordered value, 4.
options: The mean is pulled upward relative to the median.
Every value becomes equal to the mean.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.learningObjective: Apply geometric and trigonometric relationships.
questions.prompt: A right triangle has legs of length 9 and 12. What is its hypotenuse length?
questions.explanation: The hypotenuse squared is 9²+12² = 225, whose positive square root is 15.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.learningObjective: Apply geometric and trigonometric relationships.
questions.prompt: A circle has radius 5. What is its area?
questions.explanation: Area is πr² = π(5²) = 25π.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.learningObjective: Apply geometric and trigonometric relationships.
questions.prompt: Two similar triangles have corresponding side lengths in the ratio 2:3. What is the ratio of their areas in the same order?
questions.explanation: Areas scale as the square of the side-length scale factor, so 2²:3² = 4:9.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.learningObjective: Model and solve linear equations systems and inequalities.
questions.prompt: If 4(2x − 1) = 3x + 21, what is the value of x?
questions.explanation: Expand to 8x−4 = 3x+21, so 5x = 25 and x = 5.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.learningObjective: Model and solve linear equations systems and inequalities.
questions.prompt: The system x + y = 11 and x − y = 3 has solution (x, y). What is x?
questions.explanation: Add the equations to obtain 2x = 14, so x = 7.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.learningObjective: Model and solve linear equations systems and inequalities.
questions.prompt: A budget of $200 covers a fixed $35 booking fee and n tickets at $15 each. What is the greatest integer value of n allowed by the budget?
questions.explanation: 35+15n ≤ 200 gives n ≤ 11. Eleven tickets exactly meet the budget.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.learningObjective: Analyse nonlinear functions and equivalent expressions.
questions.prompt: The quadratic x² − 7x + 10 = 0 has two real solutions. What is the larger solution?
questions.explanation: Factor as (x−5)(x−2) = 0. The roots are 5 and 2, so the larger is 5.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.learningObjective: Analyse nonlinear functions and equivalent expressions.
questions.prompt: For g(x) = 2x² − 3, what is g(−2)?

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.learningObjective: Analyse nonlinear functions and equivalent expressions.
questions.prompt: A quantity doubles every 3 years. If its initial value is 40, what is its value after 9 years in this model?
questions.explanation: Nine years contains three doubling periods, so the value is 40×2³ = 320.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.learningObjective: Interpret quantitative evidence and proportional relationships.
questions.prompt: A bag contains 6 red counters and 9 blue counters, all equally likely to be selected. What is the probability of selecting a red counter? Give a fraction or decimal.
questions.explanation: There are 15 counters in total, and 6 are red. Probability = 6/15 = 2/5 = 0.4.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.learningObjective: Interpret quantitative evidence and proportional relationships.
questions.prompt: A car uses 3 gallons of fuel to travel 90 miles at a constant fuel-efficiency rate. How many gallons are needed for 240 miles at that rate?
questions.explanation: The rate is 90/3 = 30 miles per gallon. Fuel for 240 miles is 240/30 = 8 gallons.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.learningObjective: Apply geometric and trigonometric relationships.
questions.prompt: A rectangular prism has length 8, width 3 and volume 120 cubic units. What is its height?
questions.explanation: Volume = length×width×height, so height = 120/(8×3) = 5.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.learningObjective: Apply geometric and trigonometric relationships.
questions.prompt: In a right triangle, the side opposite angle θ has length 3 and the hypotenuse has length 5. What is sin θ? Give a fraction or decimal.
questions.explanation: For an acute angle in a right triangle, sine = opposite/hypotenuse = 3/5.
